tracks.title: Neurorehabilitation
tracks.tagline: Stroke recovery, spinal cord injury and traumatic brain injury.
tracks.details: Neurorehabilitation has been transformed by neuromodulation, robotics, and brain-computer interfaces translating from research into routine practice. GCPR 2027 will examine paired vagus nerve stimulation (Vivistim) for chronic upper-limb stroke deficits, robotic gait trainers (Lokomat, Andago) and soft exosuits (Wandercraft Atalante, Ekso Indego, ReWalk Personal 6.0) for ambulation recovery, and epidural and transcutaneous spinal stimulation (Onward ARC-EX, NeuroRecovery Technologies) for motor and autonomic restoration after SCI. Sessions will also cover cognitive rehabilitation after TBI, post-stroke spasticity management, and the integration of implantable BCIs (Synchron Stentrode, Neuralink, Blackrock) into communication and motor rehabilitation pathways.
subtopics: Paired VNS (Vivistim) for chronic upper-limb stroke deficits
Robotic gait training: Lokomat, Andago, Ekso Indego, ReWalk Personal 6.0
Soft exosuits: Wandercraft Atalante and overground walking outcomes
Epidural and transcutaneous spinal stimulation (Onward ARC-EX, ARC-IM)
Implantable BCIs in motor and communication rehab: Synchron, Neuralink, Blackrock
TBI cognitive rehabilitation and disorders of consciousness protocols
Spasticity management: intrathecal baclofen, onabotulinumtoxinA, cryoneurolysis

tracks.title: Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation
tracks.tagline: Sports injury, orthopedics and post-surgical recovery.
tracks.details: Musculoskeletal rehabilitation is increasingly driven by diagnostic ultrasound, regenerative interventions, and protocolized post-surgical pathways. The track will cover MSK ultrasound for dynamic joint and tendon assessment and ultrasound-guided interventions, the evolving evidence base for orthobiologics (leukocyte-poor PRP for knee OA and lateral epicondylosis, BMAC, prolotherapy), and ERAS-style protocols after total joint arthroplasty and rotator cuff repair. Sessions will also examine hydrodissection for peripheral nerve entrapments, blood-flow-restriction training in early post-operative loading, and AI-driven movement analysis (DorsaVi, Sparta, markerless 3D motion capture) for return-to-sport criteria.
subtopics: Diagnostic and interventional MSK ultrasound techniques
Orthobiologics evidence: PRP, BMAC, prolotherapy, MFAT
Blood-flow restriction training in post-surgical loading
ERAS pathways after TKA, THA, and rotator cuff repair
Hydrodissection for carpal tunnel and peripheral nerve entrapments
AI movement analysis and markerless 3D motion capture for RTS
Tendinopathy: eccentric loading, percutaneous tenotomy, shockwave

tracks.title: Cardiopulmonary Rehabilitation
tracks.tagline: Cardiac rehab, pulmonary rehab and chronic disease management.
tracks.details: Cardiopulmonary rehabilitation is being redefined by hybrid and home-based delivery models, post-COVID syndrome cohorts, and integration with disease-modifying pharmacotherapy. The track will address phase II/III cardiac rehab after PCI, CABG, TAVR, and LVAD implantation; pulmonary rehab in COPD, ILD, and post-lung-transplant populations; and structured exercise programming alongside SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 agonists. Long COVID and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 will receive dedicated sessions, including autonomic dysfunction, post-exertional malaise pacing, and graded return-to-activity protocols. Telemonitored home-based cardiac rehabilitation evidence and reimbursement pathways will be reviewed.
subtopics: Home-based and hybrid cardiac rehab: outcomes and reimbursement
Rehab after TAVR, LVAD, and heart transplantation
Pulmonary rehab in COPD, ILD, and post-lung-transplant care
Long COVID rehabilitation: autonomic dysfunction, PEM pacing
Exercise prescription with SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 agonists
CPET-guided individualized exercise prescription
Inspiratory muscle training and airway clearance techniques

tracks.title: Pediatric Rehabilitation
tracks.tagline: Developmental delays, cerebral palsy and pediatric mobility.
tracks.details: Pediatric rehabilitation has been reshaped by disease-modifying therapies in neuromuscular disease and refined surgical and pharmacologic options for cerebral palsy. The track will cover the rehabilitative implications of onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma), risdiplam, and nusinersen in SMA, exon-skipping and gene therapy in DMD (delandistrogene moxeparvovec), and longitudinal motor outcomes. CP content includes selective dorsal rhizotomy patient selection, intrathecal baclofen pump management, and single-event multilevel surgery rehabilitation. Sessions will also address constraint-induced movement therapy in hemiplegic CP, pediatric power mobility provision, and transition-of-care models from pediatric to adult rehabilitation services.
subtopics: Rehab implications of SMA therapies: onasemnogene, risdiplam, nusinersen
DMD gene therapy and exon-skipping rehabilitation outcomes
Selective dorsal rhizotomy and intrathecal baclofen in CP
Single-event multilevel surgery (SEMLS) post-op rehabilitation
Constraint-induced movement therapy in hemiplegic CP
Pediatric power mobility and seating provision
Transition of care from pediatric to adult rehabilitation

tracks.title: Geriatric Rehabilitation
tracks.tagline: Fall prevention, frailty and age-related mobility.
tracks.details: Geriatric rehabilitation sits at the intersection of sarcopenia, frailty, multimorbidity, and cognitive decline. The track will cover EWGSOP2-aligned sarcopenia diagnosis (SARC-F, grip strength, DXA), progressive resistance training and leucine-enriched protein supplementation, and the emerging pharmacologic pipeline (myostatin inhibitors, apitegromab). Falls prevention sessions will examine the Otago and STEADI programs, multifactorial assessment, and home-modification evidence. Hip fracture rehabilitation, post-ICU syndrome in older adults, and rehabilitation considerations alongside GLP-1 agonist-induced weight loss in older patients will also be addressed, along with cognitive-motor dual-task training.
subtopics: Sarcopenia diagnosis (EWGSOP2) and progressive resistance training
Frailty assessment: Fried phenotype, clinical frailty scale
Falls prevention: Otago, STEADI, multifactorial intervention
Hip fracture rehabilitation and orthogeriatric co-management
Post-ICU syndrome and ICU-acquired weakness recovery
Cognitive-motor dual-task training and dementia rehabilitation
Rehab considerations during GLP-1-induced weight loss in elders

tracks.title: Pain Management
tracks.tagline: Chronic pain, interventional pain medicine and opioid alternatives.
tracks.details: Pain medicine is being transformed by selective Nav1.8 sodium channel inhibition (suzetrigine/Journavx) for acute pain, expanded neuromodulation indications, and refined interventional techniques. The track will examine suzetrigine post-operative outcomes, low-dose ketamine infusions for refractory chronic pain and CRPS, and the maturation of dorsal root ganglion stimulation, closed-loop and high-frequency spinal cord stimulation, and peripheral nerve stimulation (Nalu, SPRINT). Interventional spine content covers cooled and conventional radiofrequency ablation for facet and SI joint pain, kyphoplasty, and minimally invasive SI joint fusion (iFuse, SI-Bone). Opioid stewardship, buprenorphine micro-induction, and cannabinoid evidence will be reviewed.
subtopics: Suzetrigine (Nav1.8 inhibition) for acute and post-operative pain
Closed-loop and high-frequency spinal cord stimulation
Dorsal root ganglion and peripheral nerve stimulation (Nalu, SPRINT)
Cooled RFA for facet and SI joint pain; genicular RFA for knee OA
Minimally invasive SI joint fusion (iFuse, SI-Bone) outcomes
Ketamine infusions in chronic pain, CRPS, and depression overlap
Buprenorphine micro-induction and opioid stewardship

tracks.title: Prosthetics & Orthotics
tracks.tagline: Smart prosthetics, exoskeletons and assistive technology.
tracks.details: Limb-loss care has advanced from socket-based prosthetics to direct skeletal attachment and intuitive neural control. The track will cover osseointegration (OPRA, OPL implants) outcomes and complication management, targeted muscle reinnervation (TMR) and targeted sensory reinnervation (TSR) for neuroma prevention and intuitive prosthetic control, and the latest mind-controlled and proprioceptive prosthetic systems including agonist-antagonist myoneural interfaces. Microprocessor knees (Ottobock Genium X4, Ossur Power Knee), powered ankles (BiOM/Empower), and bionic hands (Ottobock bebionic, Ossur i-Limb) will be benchmarked. Exoskeleton content addresses both rehabilitative and assistive personal-use devices and emerging Medicare coverage pathways.
subtopics: Osseointegration (OPRA, OPL): outcomes, infection management
TMR and TSR for neuroma prevention and intuitive control
Microprocessor knees and powered ankle-foot prostheses
Multi-articulating myoelectric hands and pattern recognition
Agonist-antagonist myoneural interface (AMI) and proprioception
Personal-use exoskeletons: ReWalk, Ekso, Atalante coverage
Pediatric prosthetic prescription and growth accommodation

tracks.title: Telerehabilitation
tracks.tagline: Remote physical therapy, wearables and digital health.
tracks.details: Telerehabilitation matured rapidly during the pandemic and is now sustained by validated digital therapeutics, wearables, and remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) reimbursement. The track will cover non-inferiority evidence for telerehab in stroke, total joint arthroplasty, and chronic low back pain; FDA-cleared digital MSK platforms (Hinge Health, Sword Health, Kaia Health); and AI-augmented home exercise adherence tools using smartphone pose estimation. Sessions will examine wearable IMU and EMG systems for remote gait and movement monitoring, asynchronous video assessment workflows, and the integration of CPT RTM codes (98975-98981) into outpatient rehab practice.
subtopics: Telerehab non-inferiority evidence in stroke, TKA, and LBP
Digital MSK platforms: Hinge Health, Sword Health, Kaia Health
Smartphone pose estimation for home exercise feedback
Wearable IMUs and surface EMG for remote movement monitoring
Remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) CPT codes and workflows
VR/AR rehabilitation: Penumbra REAL, MindMaze, XRHealth
Hybrid in-person/virtual care model design and outcomes

tracks.title: Adaptive Sports & Exercise Medicine
tracks.tagline: Paralympic medicine, adaptive fitness and return-to-play.
tracks.details: Adaptive sports medicine spans the Paralympic athlete, the recreational adaptive participant, and the role of structured exercise as medicine across disability populations. The track will cover Paralympic classification science, autonomic dysreflexia and boosting prevention in SCI athletes, thermoregulation in tetraplegia, and concussion management in adaptive sport. Sessions will examine adaptive equipment provision (racing wheelchairs, monoskis, hand-cycles), exercise prescription in MS, Parkinson disease, and post-stroke populations, and emerging high-intensity interval and resistance protocols. Return-to-play frameworks after stroke, TBI, and orthopedic injury, alongside the integration of GLP-1 agonists with exercise, will be addressed.
subtopics: Paralympic classification science and evidence-based grouping
Autonomic dysreflexia and boosting in SCI athletes
Thermoregulation strategies in tetraplegic athletes
Exercise prescription in MS, Parkinson disease, post-stroke
Adaptive equipment: racing wheelchairs, monoskis, hand-cycles
Return-to-play after stroke, TBI, and orthopedic injury
High-intensity interval training and resistance protocols in disability
